dialogue.speaker: Mark
dialogue.text: I am tired of paying rent. Do you think I should buy an apartment instead?

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: It depends on your plans. How long will you stay in this city?

dialogue.speaker: Mark
dialogue.text: At least ten years, I think. Maybe more.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Then buying could be a good investment, if you can afford it.

dialogue.speaker: Mark
dialogue.text: The problem is the mortgage. The interest rates are so high right now.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: True. Have you calculated what the monthly payments would be?

dialogue.speaker: Mark
dialogue.text: Yes, they would be slightly higher than my rent, but then the property would be mine.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: And you must add repairs, taxes and insurance to the cost.

dialogue.speaker: Mark
dialogue.text: That is a good point. With rent, the landlord pays for repairs.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Exactly, and renting is also more flexible if you change jobs.

dialogue.speaker: Mark
dialogue.text: But I feel I am throwing money away every month.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Not really. You are paying for a place to live and for the freedom to move.

dialogue.speaker: Mark
dialogue.text: I had never thought about it like that.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Compare both options on paper over fifteen years, and ask a financial adviser.

dialogue.speaker: Mark
dialogue.text: Good idea. I will make an appointment before I decide.

dialogue.speaker: You
dialogue.text: Wise. Such a big decision should never be taken in a hurry.
